title: Sum of Good Numbers
statement:
You are given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`. The element `nums[i]` is **good** when it beats both of its partners `k` steps away: it must be strictly larger than `nums[i - k]` and strictly larger than `nums[i + k]`. A partner whose index falls outside the array imposes no condition, so an element with no partner inside the array is good too.

Return the sum of all good elements of `nums`.
notes:
## Intuition

Each element is compared with at most two others, the ones exactly `k` positions to its left and right. So a single pass that checks those two positions for every index is all the problem needs; there is nothing to precompute.

## Approach

1. Start `total` at 0.
2. For each index `i`, set `beatsLeft` when `i - k` is outside the array or `nums[i] > nums[i - k]`.
3. Set `beatsRight` when `i + k` is outside the array or `nums[i] > nums[i + k]`.
4. If both hold, `nums[i]` is good: add it to `total`.
5. Return `total`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 3, 2, 1, 5, 4]`, `k = 2`.

- `i = 0` (1): no left partner, but `1 > nums[2] = 2` fails.
- `i = 1` (3): no left partner and `3 > nums[3] = 1`, so `total = 3`.
- `i = 2` (2): `2 > nums[0] = 1`, but `2 > nums[4] = 5` fails.
- `i = 3` (1): `1 > nums[1] = 3` fails.
- `i = 4` (5): `5 > nums[2] = 2` and no right partner, so `total = 8`.
- `i = 5` (4): `4 > nums[3] = 1` and no right partner, so `total = 12`.

The answer is `12`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): two comparisons per index.
- Space: O(1): only the running total.

## Pitfalls

- "Strictly larger" means a tie is not good: `[5, 5]` with `k = 1` sums to 0.
- Check the index before reading it. In JavaScript `nums[-1]` is `undefined` and `x > undefined` is false, which would wrongly reject an element with a missing partner; Java and C would read out of bounds.
- The partners are `k` steps away, not the adjacent elements (unless `k = 1`).

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `total` | sum of the good elements found so far |
| `i` | index of the element being checked |
| `beatsLeft` | `nums[i]` has no partner at `i - k` or is larger than it |
| `beatsRight` | `nums[i]` has no partner at `i + k` or is larger than it |

narration.3: Check every element of the array.
narration.4: The left partner is k steps back; if that index is outside the array there is nothing to beat.
narration.5: The same test for the right partner k steps ahead.
narration.6: An element is good only when it beats every partner that exists.
narration.7: Add the good element to the running sum.
narration.10: The sum of all good elements is the answer.
